draft.title: Functions and relations
card: Relation
A relation is any rule or set of pairs that links inputs (x values) to outputs (y values). Example: {(1, 2), (1, 5), (3, 4)}.
Function
A function is a relation where each input has exactly one output. Two different inputs may share the same output.

Check a set of pairs by looking for an x value that appears twice with different y values. If you find one, it is not a function. In the example above, x = 1 gives both 2 and 5, so it is a relation but not a function.
Vertical line test
Draw a vertical line anywhere on a graph. If some vertical line cuts the graph more than once, it is not a function. If every vertical line cuts it at most once, it is a function.
draft.remember: A function never gives two different outputs for one input.

a.q: Which set of pairs is a function?
a.why: Each x value in the first set (1, 2 and 3) has one output. Sharing the output 4 is allowed. In each other set an x value appears twice with different y values, so it has two outputs.
a.clue: Look for an x value that is repeated with different y values.

b.q: A circle on a graph is cut twice by the vertical line x = 0. What does this tell you?
opts: The circle is not the graph of a function
The circle is the graph of a function
The circle is a function only for x > 0
The circle is not a relation
b.why: A vertical line that cuts the graph twice means one x value has two y values. So it fails the vertical line test and is not a function. It is still a relation, because it pairs x values with y values.
b.clue: One vertical line cutting twice means one input has two outputs.

b.best: The circle is not the graph of a function
